newsitem.title: THAILAND: Investment board moves to promote Thai software.
newsitem.headline: Investment board moves to promote Thai software.

text.p: The Thai Board of Investment on Wednesday approved an incentive scheme, including import duty exemptions on machinery and raw materials and an eight-year corporate tax holiday, to attract computer software investment.

"The board's move is aimed at increasing the competitiveness of the country's software industry to be able to compete with neighbouring countries and to cope with its rapid growth domestically," board secretary-general Staporn Kavitanon told reporters after a meeting.
He said turnover of the Thai software market was expected to reach nine billion baht ($346 million) in 1999 from about three billion baht now.
Staporn said the incentives would apply to investment in the development of new computer software as well as the establishment of a software industrial complex.
The Board of Investment also agreed to grant investment incentives to 12 industrial projects with a total combined investment of 37.54 billion baht.
Among the projects granted promotional privileges are a hot and cold-rolled steel plant of LPN Plate Mill Co Ltd with a total investment of 10.7 billion baht.
